newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks end steady despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks end steady despite profit-taking.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed steady on buying by local institutions despite late profit-taking among cheap liquid counters on Tuesday, brokers said.

The all share index closed 0.24 points higher at 574.38. Price gains were led by blue chip holding companies Hayleys and John Keells Holdings, which rose three rupees and two rupees to 195 and 173, respectively.
"Profit-taking by retail investors among cheap liquid stocks was seen mainly in the second session," said Prasanna Chandrasekera of brokerage John Keells.
Retail investors sought profits mainly among plantation and related shares which saw significant gains last week, Chandrasekera said.
Bogawantalawa Plantation fell two rupees to 25, Kelani Valley 75 cents to 22 rupees and Tea Smallhoider Factories 1.75 rupees to 17.50.

Turnover was a moderate 19.8 million rupees. Among actives were Richard Pieris & Co, which ended unchanged at 102, Blue Diamonds, which fell 50 cents to 12.50 rupees and Dockyard which lost 25 cents to 10.75 rupees.
